questions.explanation: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid. It is the molecule that carries the genetic instructions for the development, functioning, and reproduction of all living organisms.

questions.stem: What is the shape of the DNA molecule?
questions.explanation: DNA has a double helix structure, like a twisted ladder. The two strands are held together by complementary base pairs and twist around each other. This structure was discovered by Watson and Crick in 1953.

questions.stem: Which base pairs with adenine (A) in DNA?
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T), and cytosine (C) always pairs with guanine (G). This is called complementary base pairing and is held together by hydrogen bonds.

questions.stem: What are the three components of a DNA nucleotide?

options.text: A protein, a lipid, and a carbohydrate
An amino acid, a sugar, and a phosphate
A phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and a base
A ribose sugar, a phosphate, and an enzyme

questions.explanation: Each DNA nucleotide consists of three parts: a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and one of four nitrogenous bases (adenine, thymine, cytosine, or guanine). The phosphate and sugar form the backbone of the DNA strand.

questions.stem: What type of bond holds the two strands of DNA together?

options.text: Hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs

questions.explanation: The two strands of DNA are held together by hydrogen bonds between the complementary base pairs (A-T and C-G). These bonds are relatively weak individually, allowing the strands to separate during replication and protein synthesis.

questions.stem: If one strand of DNA has the base sequence ATCGGA, what is the complementary sequence on the other strand?
questions.explanation: Using complementary base pairing rules (A pairs with T, C pairs with G): A-T, T-A, C-G, G-C, G-C, A-T. So the complementary strand is TAGCCT.

questions.stem: Where is DNA found in a eukaryotic cell?

options.text: In the nucleus (and small amounts in mitochondria)

questions.explanation: In eukaryotic cells, the vast majority of DNA is found in the nucleus, organised into chromosomes. Small amounts of DNA are also found in mitochondria (and chloroplasts in plant cells), which have their own circular DNA.
